newsitem.title: BULGARIA: European Union pledges to support Bulgaria reforms.
newsitem.headline: European Union pledges to support Bulgaria reforms.

text.p: A senior European Union official on Tuesday pledged support for Bulgaria to help the government implement a reform programme agreed with the International Monetary Fund.

"We know that the population is going through difficult times and a difficult reform process is to be established, but we believe confidence in the government is great, which is also reflected in yesterday's agreement in principle with the International Monetary Fund," EU External Affairs Commissioner Hans van den Broek told reporters.
On Monday, the IMF and the interim government announced a new standby accord and an emergency payment to buy grain, totalling more than $650 million.

The interim cabinet, in office until after elections on April 19, committed itself to strict financial discipline to prepare for implementation of a fixed exchange rate regime by the new government in June.
The interim cabinet has the support of the Union of Democratic Forces, which is expected to form the next government.
The programme must be approved by the IMF board next month, and Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski will leave for Washington on Tuesday evening to support Bulgaria's case.
A Consultative Group meeting of lenders will take place in Brussels in early April.

"We have committed ourselves with the prime minister to mobilise international support for providing economic assistance in which the European Union will substantially participate," Van den Broek said.
Sofianski made a televised address on Monday night explaining the agreement and preparing the population for more financial hardship.

He said the agreement would open the door to negotiations with the World Bank on a $300 million loan, but warned 58,000 public sector workers would be laid off in the transitional period. He said Bulgaria would receive some $120 million outside the IMF agreement for severance payments.
Electricity prices would rise again by between 30 and 60 percent in the coming months and central heating prices would also gradually rise.
As a first step towards price liberalisation, prices of agricultural products and import and export regulations on them would be decontrolled.
Sofianski said after talks with Van den Broek the European Union could provide more income support for the poorest Bulgarians.
A handout of 20 million ECUs ($22.8 million) of PHARE programme money for the poorest households and institutions such as orphanages and homes for the handicapped is due to be disbursed next week.

Sofianski said their talks had also covered safety at the Kozloduy nuclear plant and the question of intellectual property. Bulgaria is the world's second largest producer of pirate compact discs after China. ($ = 0.875 European Currency Unit ECUs)
